page_title: Stelix · Live stem separation for your Mac

sources.entry: Stelix - Live stem separation for your Mac: splits what any app is playing into vocals, drums, bass and other in real time, so you can turn each one up or down or hear it alone, all on-device. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/stelix-app/stelix) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Stelix
summary.one_liner: Stelix is a free, open-source Mac app that splits whatever audio your Mac is playing into vocals, drums, bass and other stems in real time, or separates a recorded file into six stems.
use_cases: Removing vocals from a song to sing or play along karaoke-style
Isolating drums, bass or other instruments to practice with
Splitting a recorded file into six stems for study
Turning down one instrument while listening to any app's audio
Saving separated vocals and instrumentals as WAV files
summary.what_it_does: Live mode captures whatever any app on the Mac is playing and separates it into four stems (vocals, drums, bass, other) about one second behind the audio, with per-stem sliders, solo, and presets such as Vocals Only and No Vocals. Studio mode, or drag-and-drop of an audio file, separates a recording into six stems (vocals, piano, guitar, bass, drums, other) that can be played in a built-in player and saved as WAV files. The page says audio is processed entirely on-device, with no account or telemetry. Separation uses neural network models that the app downloads on request, and it shows a tempo readout on macOS 27 and later.
notable: Live real-time separation of any app's audio with no audio driver to install
Fully on-device processing; no account, analytics or telemetry
GPL-3.0 open source with code on GitHub
Not notarized by Apple; a one-time manual approval step is required to open it
caveats: Requires a Mac with Apple silicon; Intel Macs and Windows/iOS are not supported
Requires macOS 15 or later; only macOS 27 has been tested so far
Neural network models (about 2.3 GB) are not included and their licenses are unclear, some possibly non-commercial; intended for personal use
Live mode needs a fast GPU and may not run on slower Macs such as the MacBook Air M2 at the Pro level
